title: Adaptive opset-drift detection and staged fallback policy for quantized-serving instability
creator: Avery Chen
description: Post-incident follow-up for a multi-region outage where quantized model deployments entered a crash/restart loop and produced silent accuracy drift. This ticket synthesizes the root cause, detection gaps, and a concrete set of mitigations that minimize customer impact during mixed-precision and opset transitions.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-10 02:13 UTC: Canary job for model-preview-3 began reporting increased op latency and kernel fallbacks in us-west-2.

2026-03-10 02:18 UTC: Autoscaler responded to increased tail latency by provisioning additional GPU pods; shortly after, some pods entered crash loops due to repeated eviction and OOM in quant runtime.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC: Console alerts escalated to on-call. Initial hypothesis pointed at KV cache corruption; mitigation attempted: forced cache eviction and restart of affected pods.
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC: Eviction + restart made situation worse: restart thrash caused host-level CPU contention, causing canary to keep failing and triggering further autoscale churn.
2026-03-10 04:10 UTC: Hot-fix rollback to float32 variant reduced failures but downstream customers reported small but measurable semantic output shifts vs baseline prompts.

2026-03-11 09:30 UTC: Post-incident analysis began; initial logs showed a sequence of unsupported fused ops (fast_gelu variants) that were silently mapped to a slow, emulated kernel path in the quant runtime which changed numerical ordering leading to drift.
2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: Reproduction confirmed on staging with a model containing operator pattern conv->fast_gelu->layernorm when converted with model-converter v2.3.2.
2026-03-12 15:25 UTC: Decision to implement adaptive detection + staged fallback rather than blanket rollback across all quant deployments.
root_cause: A converter-induced opset pattern (fused fast_gelu variant) caused runtime kernel selection to pick a slow, emulated quant kernel with a different numerical evaluation order. The mismatch triggered micro-evictions in runtime memory heuristics and produced subtle token-distribution shifts (accuracy drift). Autoscaler + restart logic amplified the capacity spike into crash/restart oscillation.
detection: Existing observability captured latency and pod restarts but lacked: (1) per-op fingerprinting to detect incompatible fused ops early, (2) a canary-level semantic-eval that would have surfaced distributional drift, (3) circuit-breaker metrics to stop autoscaling in reaction to runtime thrash.
mitigation_summary: We will introduce lightweight per-model opset fingerprinting at converter-time, a scoring function to decide between quant-compatibility, soft-fallback to a quant-safe kernel, or automatic promotion to float variant. Additionally, implement autoscaler safety gates and KV cache eviction backoff to avoid restart amplification.
action_items: A1: Add per-model opset fingerprint during converter pipeline that emits a 'compat_score' string and a list of suspect op patterns. Owner: converter team. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-22.

A2: Implement adaptive fallback policy in runtime: scoring thresholds (green/yellow/red) to choose fast quant kernel, quant-safe emulation with monitoring, or float fallback. Owner: serving-runtime. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-04-05.

A3: Instrument a lightweight semantic canary for every canary job that evaluates 50 templated prompts and computes distribution distance vs baseline (KL + token edit). Fail canary on >threshold drift. Owner: e2e-testing. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-26.
A4: Autoscaler safety gate: do not autoscale up in a region if restart rate > X restarts/min or if pod CPU steal > 20%. Owner: infra-autoscale. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-20.

A5: Backoff eviction policy for KV cache: exponential backoff combined with graceful degradation mode to accept slight latency increases instead of immediate full-restart. Owner: runtime-memory. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-29.
A6: Create regression evals for fused-op patterns and add to nightly quant-canaries. Owner: applied-ml. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-24.
A7: Postmortem doc and customer comms template for quant regressions. Owner: support-eng. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-18.
A8: Add operator-level telemetry (op fingerprint counts) to Console dashboards and set alerting on sudden spikes of 'unknown-op' in quant path. Owner: observability. Estimate: 4. Due: 2026-03-25.
A9: Manual remediation runbook (playbook) for on-call to safely drain and promote float variants without triggering autoscale. Owner: SRE. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-16.

A10: Run a limited cohort of customers through staged rollouts with the adaptive fallback enabled and collect quality and cost metrics for 2 weeks before general release. Owner: product-ops. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-04-12.

A11: Add conversion-time validation that warns and blocks converter versions known to produce the fused-op pattern unless an explicit opt-in is provided. Owner: converter. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-21.
A12: Schedule a cross-team tech review and tabletop for similar incidents; include SRE, Runtime, Converter, Autoscale, and Applied ML. Owner: eng-ops. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-19.
A13: Implement a canary rollback decorator in the deployment system to automatically pause rollouts when canary semantic drift is detected. Owner: rollout-service. Estimate: 4. Due: 2026-04-02.
A14: Post-deployment metric review at +1 week and +4 weeks that tracks semantic drift, op-fallback rate, and restart churn. Owner: product-analytics. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-04-05.
A15: Add unit tests for quant kernel deterministic ordering to the kernel-suite. Owner: kernel-team. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-30.
metrics_observed: Peak pod restarts: +720% on affected canaries
Tail latency (p99): increased by 180ms baseline -> +80ms during fallback
KV cache eviction rate: 4x increase during incident
Semantic drift signal (ad-hoc): KL divergence ~0.07 on prompt set for affected model
Autoscale churn: 3 extra scale-up events in 45 minutes per region
